questions.question: What does it mean that $M$ is an upper bound for a set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$?
options: For every $x\in E$, $x\leq M$.
For every $x\in E$, $M\leq x$.
There exists $x\in E$ such that $x = M$.
$M$ is the only real number related to $E$.

questions.question: Does an upper bound of $E$ have to belong to $E$?
options: No, an upper bound need not belong to the set.
Yes, every upper bound must be an element of the set.
Only if the set is empty.
Only if the set has exactly one element.

options: $\frac12$

questions.question: How is an upper bound different from an element of a set?
options: An upper bound must be one of the elements of the set.
An upper bound restricts the set from above and may lie outside the set.
An upper bound is always smaller than every element of the set.
An upper bound is defined only for finite sets.
